note: Divergence ratchets for scripts/flix-spec-conformance.mjs. Lower them as divergences are fixed; never raise one without saying why in the commit message. The measurement is only comparable against the flix-spec inputs recorded below -- a different pin or fixture revision is a different question, not a regression. Two ratchets, because there are two derived lanes: `divergences` gates structure modulo error recovery, and `recoveryDivergences` gates error-recovery shape on its own. NOTE: agreement fell from 122 to 107 when the mapping set was completed, because unmapped nodes are skipped rather than compared -- depth rose 84% to 90%. Read fixturesAgreeing together with depthPercent; a high agreement count at low depth is the number to distrust.

oracle_conformance.comment: Re-measured against flix-spec 0.75.8, which pins Flix v0.75.2. This is a different question from the previous baseline, not a regression against it: the suite grew 136 -> 138 fixtures, Decl.Law left the inventory when Flix removed law declarations, and two flix-spec fixes changed what the numbers mean. divergenceCount is no longer truncated at twenty per fixture, and depth is now measured against the expectation rather than against wherever the walk stopped -- which is why depth reads 95% here against 99% before while nothing about this grammar got worse. law_declaration moved from mappings to ignored: its canonical counterpart no longer exists.

recovery_conformance.comment: Error-recovery shape alone, over the 22 fixtures whose raw reference tree contains a recovery marker. The 69% depth is the corrected metric showing what it always should have: a large part of each recovering tree sits under a node this map has no opinion about, and the old denominator hid exactly that. The dominant disagreement is unchanged and diagnosed in flix-spec's docs/CONFORMANCE.md: both parsers reject `1_`, and they disagree about where the error is.

source_invariants.comment: document-shape passes. The two vocabulary checks stand down because a projection map is in play, and token-accounting stands down because this adapter emits no token text -- tree-sitter's named-node view has no Flix tokenization behind it. A structural profile, stated rather than implied.
